key_insight: Train two separate LLMs — a Code LLM and a Test LLM — in an adversarial, co-evolving reinforcement learning loop so tests become progressively harder and code generation becomes more robust, avoiding trivial test generation or generic low-coverage suites.
problem_solved: Addresses brittle RL rewards for code generation caused by scarce/high-quality unit tests and the self-collusion dilemma of single-model self-play (trivial tests from white‑box access vs. generic weak tests under black‑box constraints).
method: Adversarial co-evolution: alternate/update a Test LLM that generates unit tests and a Code LLM that attempts to solve them, forming a competitive training loop.

Reinforcement learning with dynamic rewards: use execution-based signals (test pass/fail, coverage, difficulty) and diversity/hardness bonuses to adapt rewards as models improve and prevent trivialization.

Population/curriculum and access control: maintain evolving model populations or constrained interfaces (graded white/gray/black-box) to reduce self-collusion and encourage generalizable test/code behaviors.
impact: Delivers stronger, automatically generated test suites and more robust code LLMs by replacing static, scarce rewards with an adaptive adversarial signal — improving RL training quality and real-world reliability of code generation systems.

Pipeline flowchart: test generation → code generation → execution → reward computation → RL update (highlighting dynamic reward components).

paper_title: Code-A1: Adversarial Evolving of Code LLM and Test LLM via Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Aozhe Wang, Yuchen Yan, Nan Zhou, Zhengxi Lu, Weiming Lu
